Hollow-point rounds are good for reducing the incidence of bystander injuries. They are less likely to pass through the target, as an FMJ round may. The reason that they are not permitted under the Hague Convention is more to do with the dated characteristics of war, whereby the objectives are to tie up your opponent, forcing resources to deal with injured comrades and thereby reducing efficiencies on the battlefield. There's also the reasoning that war should "kill" as few people as possible. I know it may sound crazy, but the concept is that "we don't want to kill you all, we just want to conquer you in a manner that will make it economically and socially expensive for you to continue to fight". Anyway, hollow-point rounds are a better round for home/self defence since they will not be so likely to pass through a partition wall and penetrate into someone more welcome. It may also be argued that law enforcement benefit because the rounds are less likely to cause injury to non-involved members of the public. That being said, we all know exactly how law enforcement agencies around the world now operate (them vs us) and providing these psychopaths with anything more than a pea-shooter is just asking for a blood-bath.
